subject: Clarifying data-retention windows and explicit non-training warranty for FinAnalytics
messages:
From: Jacob Lane <jacob.lane@finanalytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick confirmation: do you ever use our request/response data for model training?

Hi Evelyn,

Hope you're well. We're finalizing procurement paperwork and have a gating question from legal/security: can Redwood provide a clear, written commitment that customer request/response content (payloads) is not used to train production models or otherwise incorporated into model training datasets?

A few specifics they'd like clarified:
- Are short-term logs or debug snapshots ever sampled for offline model tuning or R&D?
- What are the default retention windows for request/response content vs telemetry/metrics vs backups/snapshots?
- For Hosted API customers, do you offer an option to opt-out of any retention beyond immediate processing?

If possible, can you attach any attestation or SOC2 excerpt we can pass to procurement? We have a tight timeline on our PO (EOD next Thu).

Thanks,
Jacob
Jacob Lane
Head of Security, FinAnalytics
jacob.lane@finanalytics.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-14T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick confirmation: do you ever use our request/response data for model training?

Hi Jacob — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and I attached two artifacts for procurement: a signed attestation template and a compact retention matrix.

Short answers (summary):
- We do not use customer request/response content to train or fine-tune any production or research models. That includes any verbatim prompts, responses, or transcripts submitted through the Hosted API.
- Short-term operational logs and telemetry (e.g., error traces, latency histograms) may be retained and occasionally analyzed in aggregate for product reliability; these telemetry signals are not fed into model training datasets.
- Default retention windows (Hosted API):
  * Customer content (payloads): 30 days for troubleshooting by default, unless a customer selects a longer/shorter policy via account settings or contract.
  * Operational telemetry/metrics: 90 days by default for diagnostics/observability.
  * Backups & snapshots: up to 365 days (encrypted), with a tombstone workflow to delete customer-associated snapshots on request.

Notes and nuances:
- Private/Dedicated deployments: customers elect data residency and retention; many customers deploy with a zero-retention (no persistent logs) configuration. For those deployments there is an explicit "no-retain" flag and we will not store payloads beyond ephemeral memory on the serving hosts.
- Anonymized, aggregated telemetry: We may use non-identifying aggregate metrics to improve runtime performance (e.g., batching heuristics); we do not use any content-derived signals that could reproduce user-provided content in models.
- Debug snapshots: snapshots created for debugging are encrypted and access-controlled; they are routinely rotated and can be excluded from retention entirely by contract.

I've attached: redwood-no-train-attestation.pdf (fillable attestation), retention-matrix-2028.csv (concise tables), and a small SOC2 controls excerpt that highlights evidence sources. Marcus and Priyom are looped in for any legal/ops detail.

If you'd like, Marcus can provide the formal legal wording we typically ship in SOWs and Priyom can confirm the operational removal path (API / ticket / DocuSign). Happy to hop on a short call this week.

Best,
Evelyn

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick confirmation: do you ever use our request/response data for model training?

Jacob — looping in the legal/ops clarification. Short legal/operational confirmation below; consider this language suitable to include in procurement attachments.

Formalized confirmation (suitable for PO):
- Redwood does not use customer-submitted content (requests, responses, transcripts) to train, fine-tune, or benchmark any of its production or research language models unless the customer provides explicit, documented consent.
- Debug snapshots, logs, and backups are strictly access-controlled and are not part of any model training pipelines. There are no automated jobs that move customer content from operational backups into model training datasets.
- Aggregated telemetry may be used to improve infrastructure and runtime optimizations; such telemetry is non-content (metrics, counters, latency distributions) and cannot be transformed to reconstruct original customer content.

Operational remedies and customer options:
- We will sign the attestation and return it as a DocuSign package (see attached sample signed file for format).
- For Hosted customers, you may request (via the support API or via signed contract addendum) that payload retention be set to zero, enable additional encryption-at-rest controls, and request periodic destruction of snapshots tied to your account.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments, we support configurations that keep no persistent customer payloads beyond processing memory.

If you want formal wording inserted into your PO, use the paragraph above. We're happy to supply a signed PDF within 24 business hours once procurement sends the DocuSign envelope.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
